title: Don't Toss That Old Kindle! Turn It Into a Spotify Remote, Smart Display, or Literary Clock
summary: Do you have an old Amazon Kindle lying around? Maybe you got a new one and aren't sure what to do with the old one. Don't throw it away! Those e-readers are actually super versatile, and with a little tinkering, you can turn them into something totally new and cool. Here are three fun projects to try. First, you can use your Kindle as a Spotify remote! No, you won't be downloading the Spotify app or storing songs on it. Instead, you'll use a feature called Spotify Connect. Once you set it up, your Kindle can control music playing on another device, like your phone or laptop. You can skip tracks, pause, and resume playback right from the Kindle's screen. It's like having a dedicated music controller that's easy on the eyes. All you need is to enter your Spotify info and make sure both devices are on the same Wi-Fi. Second, you can transform your Kindle into a smart display. This one is a bit more involved, but it's really rewarding. You can set it up to show all sorts of useful information: weather forecasts, your calendar, to-do lists, and even delivery status updates. Developer Matt Healy has shared full instructions online. You'll need to do some coding and maybe even build a custom frame, but by the end, you'll have a sleek, always-on display that pulls data from different services. It's a great way to learn about hardware hacking and how apps talk to each other. Third, you can turn your Kindle into a literary clock. This hack keeps the book theme but turns the device into a clock that shows a different quote from a book for each minute of the day. There are 1,440 minutes in a day, so that's a lot of quotes! The good news is that all the images and scripts have already been prepared, so you just need to follow the instructions. The clock doesn't show the book title or author, so it doubles as a fun literary quiz—you can press the screen to reveal the answer. Whether you want a music remote, a smart display, or a clock that speaks in book quotes, your old Kindle can do it. So grab that dusty device and start hacking!
why_it_matters: Instead of throwing away old gadgets, you can turn them into something useful and learn valuable tech skills—it's like giving your device a second life.

background_read: The Amazon Kindle (an e-reader for books from the company Amazon) has been around since 2007, and many people upgrade to newer models.
Old Kindles use special screens that are easy on the eyes, making them perfect for displaying text even when they can't run the latest apps anymore.
By repurposing them, you help reduce electronic waste and get a fun project that teaches you about technology.
Article_Structure: WHO: Owners of old Amazon Kindles and tech-savvy hobbyists.
WHAT: Three projects to turn an old Kindle into a Spotify remote, a smart display, or a literary clock.
WHERE: Anywhere with Wi-Fi and a bit of curiosity.
WHY: Because old devices still have value and can be turned into useful tools, and it's a fun way to learn about technology.

perspectives.description: Repurposing old devices is creative, eco-friendly, and a great way to learn coding and hardware skills.
Taking apart gadgets can be risky and might break them, so not everyone should try it, and you could lose your data.
These projects are for hobbyists who enjoy Do-It-Yourself challenges, but they require patience and carefully following instructions.
